requirements.title: Logical literals use complete dotted TRUE or FALSE spellings with an optional kind suffix
requirements.definition: A logical literal has the complete .TRUE. or .FALSE. spelling and may have an underscore followed by kind-param. The canonical letter rule permits corresponding lower and mixed case outside character contexts. The suffix syntax is R709, not an arbitrary kind-selector expression. I/O abbreviations do not add logical-literal spellings to program source.

pending.digit-suffix: Phase 2: independently supported static branches 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 admit both literal values with digit suffixes, including one zero-padded spelling.

requirements.oracle: Compile controls cover complete spellings, named default suffixes and case variants. Four one-defect DATA pairs check abbreviated true/false, a missing closing dot and an empty suffix. The target's exact defined-operator token, unrecognized-dot and orphan-underscore routes distinguish those lexical defects; GNU's missing-kind-parameter route also qualifies the genuinely empty suffix. Generic DATA/expected-values recovery is not credited.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R709/C718/C719 retain literal-kind grammar, named-constant type/constancy and sign ownership; R704/R706/C717 retain declaration selectors. A unary minus or relational comparison of logical values is not manufactured as a logical-literal negative. Only cause-specific located token routes qualify; generic logical/type/constant/kind nouns, unsupported language facilities, crashes, verifier and resource failures cannot pass. Reporting may be nonfatal when specifically qualified.
requirements.dependencies: 6.1.2 p3 and S6.1.2-002, PDF 67; R709/C718/C719, PDF 80-81; 8.6.7/R848 and p8/p10, PDF 137-138; C733; 4.2 p2(3), PDF 46. Formatted/list-directed input syntax is not the source-literal grammar.

requirements.title: A logical literal kind value identifies an available logical method
requirements.definition: The kind-param of a logical literal identifies a logical representation method available on the processor. The condition applies to either truth-value spelling and to digit-string or named selectors. A nonnegative number need not be supported, and support for the same number as an integer or real kind does not establish logical support.
requirements.oracle: Four isolated compile-only pairs use nonnegative unsupported logical kind zero and minimal supported repairs. The unchanged LOGICAL_KINDS profile establishes absence without compiling the candidate. Flang's explicit LOGICAL(KIND=0) report qualifies. GNU's observed full logical-constant bad-kind report was checked against its kind-value validation path, distinct from preceding selector parsing; the exact literal point and already-constant zero parameter bind the value. The target's undeclared-variable-zero report and silent named-zero acceptance do not qualify.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Zero is not universally unsupported and may be a valid kind value. If it is supported, this finite negative family is unavailable rather than passing; the mandatory named controls still run. A later independently qualified absent code can extend the finite family without claiming all integers were searched. C719 owns negative kind values. Do not exclude all unsupported messages: distinguish unsupported kind values from unimplemented facilities, parser recovery, already-constant-expression errors, crashes, ASR verifier and resource failures.
requirements.dependencies: R725/R709/C718/C719; 16.10.2.20 LOGICAL_KINDS, PDF 475; 16.9.118 KIND, PDF 424; 4.2 p2(3)-(4), PDF 46. Existing profile: tests/profiles/integer_literal_absent_zero_logical.f90. Declaration support remains C717.

requirements.title: Logical methods represent true and false as logical values
requirements.definition: The two logical values represent truth and falsity. Their meaning is independent of the chosen logical kind and is not an integer-value, bit-pattern or storage-size convention. The domain statement does not license inspecting undefined logical storage or invent a third logical value from a transferred bit pattern.

pending.selected-truth-values: Phase 2: run the same two-value checks for every method in the at-most-sixteen-entry LOGICAL_KINDS witness. Selected/default kind aliases are valid.
pending.kind-independent-values: Phase 2: a separately qualified pair of distinct logical kinds, if available, carries true and false through same-value logical assignment and checks truth with an explicitly declared dummy of each kind. The single-method case remains conforming; do not require a second kind.

requirements.oracle: Exact logical truth assertions observe values directly. Cross-kind assignment is only a dependent context for preservation of the two values, not an attempt to own the whole assignment rule or establish storage compatibility.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The finite checks do not claim to test every stored bit pattern. Uninitialized values, raw integer aliases, TRANSFER encodings and assumptions that true equals one or minus one are excluded. Code must not rely on short-circuit evaluation to make an invalid branch safe. These are runtime effects even when a compiler lacks a selected logical method.
requirements.dependencies: 10.1.5.4.1 and its logical truth tables, PDF 179; 10.2.1.3 p10, PDF 191; 16.10.2.20, PDF 475. The two-value domain is separately classified as a definition.

requirements.title: One or more logical methods are identified by KIND
requirements.source: 7.4.5 p2, PDF 87, printed 73, lines 9-11, excluding the separately linked default-integer parameter-type restatement.
requirements.definition: At least one logical representation method is available. Each method is identified by a KIND value, and KIND returns that parameter for an entity of the method. The default-integer type of the parameter named KIND is already owned by S7.4.1-001; its numeric identifier is not a portable representation description.

pending.finite-method-inventory: Phase 2: a separate at-most-sixteen-entry inventory witness instantiates every advertised logical method and tests both literal values and KIND identity. Guard empty inventories and constant indices; more than sixteen methods needs an explicit follow-on family, not silently truncated evidence.

requirements.oracle: Runtime inventory membership, explicit type/kind agreement and both truth values establish a finite supported-method witness. A bounded inventory entry is selected without assuming order or a numeric code, and no distinct-kind assertion is made unless the profile establishes it.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The logical type need not have multiple kinds. Kind codes may coincide numerically with integer/real codes without making their types interchangeable. A failed advertised method is a failed effect, not a profile skip based on missing compiler facilities. Inquiry results and actual truth values do not promise a specific bit layout.
requirements.dependencies: 7.4.1 p2/S7.4.1-001, PDF 80; 16.9.118, PDF 424; 16.10.2.20, PDF 475; 10.1.12, PDF 187-188, permits constant inquiry and array-constant-subobject selectors.

requirements.title: A LOGICAL declaration without a selector has the kind of the default false literal
requirements.definition: LOGICAL without a kind-selector denotes default logical, with the kind value KIND(.FALSE.). This declaration-default rule is separate from the grammar of LOGICAL and from the kind of a literal assigned to the object.
requirements.oracle: The declaration's inquiry and an explicit matching dummy supply the exact type/kind oracle. No numeric kind code or storage-sized constant is required.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R704/R706/C717 retain declaration syntax and support ownership. Assignment can convert a logical value from another kind and therefore cannot alone establish the literal's original kind. No default kind is assumed to be one, four or any other fixed number.
requirements.dependencies: R704/R706/C717, PDF 80; 16.9.118, PDF 424; 10.2.1.3 p10, PDF 191; 15.5.2.5 supplies explicit intrinsic dummy agreement.

requirements.title: A logical literal takes its explicit suffix kind or the default logical kind
requirements.definition: A logical literal with a kind suffix has the specified supported logical kind. Without that suffix it has default logical kind. Both truth-value spellings obey the same rule. Selected kind values can coincide; different selector spellings need not mean different representations.

pending.named-true: Following bounded pass: check .TRUE._lk for every method in the complete bounded logical inventory, including independently qualified nondefault methods. The authored default-only subset has its own default-named-true facet and does not close this full-inventory plan.
pending.named-false: Following bounded pass: repeat direct-literal kind and truth checks for .FALSE._lk over the complete bounded inventory. The default-named-false subset is separately credited; remaining methods are explicitly pending.
pending.digit-suffixed: Phase 2: use independently supported static code branches 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 for both values, including a zero-padded spelling. No branch infers support from integer or real inventories.

requirements.oracle: The unprofiled run cases inquire KIND on both unsuffixed literals and on named default-kind true/false literals before assignment, with logical truth and explicit dummy checks. An alias case uses two names for the same supported default kind and separately named procedures. The two added default-named facets identify the bounded subset without closing the original full-inventory named-true/named-false plans.
requirements.oracle_limitation: R709 owns suffix spelling alternatives and C733 owns support. These value/kind effects do not establish byte counts, true/false integer encodings or a kind relation to other intrinsic types. The finite numeric-code family can be unavailable on a conforming processor; unprofiled named/default cases still apply and broader numeric spelling coverage remains bounded.
requirements.dependencies: R725/C733 and R709/C718/C719, PDF 87 and 80-81; 16.9.118, PDF 424; 16.10.2.20, PDF 475; 10.2.1.3 p10, PDF 191, separates subsequent assignment conversion.

accounting.rationale: PDF 87 line 8 supplies the two-value domain and the meanings of the two values.
Logical has exactly two values. This is a semantic domain, not a license to enumerate arbitrary object-representation bits or read undefined storage.
PDF 87 lines 9-11 separates method existence/representation, KIND characterization, the parameter's default-integer type and the KIND inquiry.
PDF 87 lines 13-14 preserves the absent-selector condition and the exact default-kind inquiry.
PDF 87 lines 18-19 distinguishes the explicit kind suffix from its omission.

review_rationale: Independent source-plan and fixture review with verified corrections: doc/source_audits/batch_010.json. Required logical methods/truth/inquiries and literal controls are eligible. Default-only named facets are separated from the still-pending full-inventory forms. Unsupported zero is independently qualified, not universally forbidden.
